approach: Two changes at the source, plus a correct lifecycle for the new hold. (1) Reclaim: disk.rs gets `sweep_interrupted_targets` and `Athena::reclaim_interrupted`. They remove only `target/` of jobs that are Dispatched in Records, have no registry entry after `reap()`, are not on the keep list, and whose job lock `try_lock_job` can take (held while removing). drain.rs gets a defaulted `Steps::reclaim_interrupted(own)`, called at drain start with an empty keep list and in `run_job` right before `steps.run`, with the drain's own jobs as keep list. (2) Pre-producer gate: `producer_disk_gate` in run/producer.rs (one `disk_gate` call), called from `produce_and_verify` right after `baseline_stage` and before the work tree and snapshot exist. On low space it returns `Err(self.hold_for_disk(ctx, closing, low))`. (3) Hold lifecycle (answers finding 1): a job held before the producer has no resume mark, so the existing spend path (`consumed_resume`) never clears its marker. `dispatch` gets a small `release_superseded_hold` called on the non-resume path: when the request is "try again on X", X is Dispatched, not running, has a hold marker and no resume mark, X's marker is cleared once the retry has committed its dispatch. The `go` refusal at run/mod.rs:346 names a re-read, not a resume, when there is no resume mark. Docs of `hold_for_disk` (close.rs) and the drain's interrupted bullet name the third caller. All behavior tests go in the existing integration file crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs; no `#[path]` include, no stub Job record.

decisions.reason: Root cause: nothing checked space between the baseline build (which fills the disk) and the producer; the dispatch gate (run/mod.rs:749) runs earlier. `produce_and_verify` owns `closing` by value, which `hold_for_disk` (close.rs:176) takes; the Err flows through `finish_dispatched` as the check-gate hold at run/mod.rs:1303 does. The work tree does not exist yet, so nothing needs cleanup. The gate sweeps idle targets first and keeps the job's own, like the other gates.

rejected.option: Gate at the top of `producer_loop`'s pass (covers send-back reruns)
rejected.why: `producer_loop` holds `&mut Closing`, `hold_for_disk` needs it by value; fixing that needs a new Flow variant or more of close.rs. A send-back rerun follows a producer that already ran, and the gate before the checks (run/mod.rs:1301) still covers its built candidate.
The baseline is recorded only and never stops a job; its own build is what lowers space just before the producer.
`enter` returns `()`, so it cannot hold a job.

decisions.choice: Answer finding 1: give the pre-producer hold a lifecycle. In `dispatch` (run/mod.rs), on the non-resume path (right after `let mut closing = Closing::new();`, so only when `resume_from` is None and after the prediction commit), call new `release_superseded_hold(records, request_text, &id)`. It reads `retried_job(records, request_text)`; if that job is not the new one, is `JobState::Dispatched`, is not `self.running(..)`, has a hold marker and `self.state.read_resume(..)` is None, it calls `clear_hold(old)`. Also change the `go` refusal at run/mod.rs:346-351: with a resume mark it keeps the 'resumes it from its kept candidate' text; without one it says 'A drain reads it again once space is free'.
decisions.reason: Read: `clear_hold` at run/mod.rs:762 clears only the new job's id; the old marker is cleared only through `closing.consumed_resume` (close.rs:195, run/mod.rs:590), set only in `resume_candidate` (:524) from a resume mark. A job held before the producer has none, so its marker would stay and status.rs:1662 would show 'low disk' on it for good. The retry knows its source from the request text, so the retry spends the marker once it has dispatched (its prediction commit is made; the source is superseded). The `read_resume` guard leaves the existing late-hold path (marker plus a resume mark whose seed was rejected) exactly as it is.

rejected.option: Set `closing.consumed_resume` to the held job on the non-resume path
rejected.why: `settle_resume_marks` and `hold_for_disk` would also `remove_resume(old)`, deleting a resume mark whose seed was rejected for a base change; that is a behavior change outside the scope.

rejected.option: Clear the marker before the retry commits (right after `resume_seed`)
rejected.why: A dispatch that fails at preflight or the commit would then lose the marker while the job stays interrupted and unrecorded.

rejected.option: Write a resume mark with no candidate at the pre-producer hold
rejected.why: `resume_seed` needs a candidate commit; a candidate-less mark is a new state across state.rs, retry and the drain, which is a larger change.

rejected.option: Hold before the dispatch commit instead (job stays Proposed)
rejected.why: The prediction commit and the baseline run before the gate; moving the gate before them defeats its purpose (the baseline build is what lowers space).

decisions.choice: Reclaim `target/` only, via `StateDir::remove_target`, for jobs Dispatched in Records with no registry entry (after `registry().reap()`), outside the keep list and whose `try_lock_job` succeeds. Check cheap predicates first, then the lock, so closed jobs get no lock file. `Athena::reclaim_interrupted` loads Records once; a failed head or load prints a `warning:` line and returns 0.
decisions.reason: The brief keeps work trees and candidates. status.rs:1615-1616 already calls Dispatched-and-not-running 'interrupted'. `go_job` takes the job lock before the Dispatched commit (run/mod.rs:308), so the lock covers the window the registry misses.

rejected.why: Filtered to drained channels and drops jobs a retry already names; some interrupted directories would stay.
Deletes the work tree; out of scope.

rejected.option: Sweep every unlocked dir like sweep_idle_targets

decisions.choice: Answer finding 3: the keep list in `run_job` is exactly `read.job` (the id passed to `steps.run`, a new id after a retry) plus the `job` field of every `JobLine` already pushed in `self.st().jobs` (the jobs this drain has already run or held). The queue key `item.job` and `st.tried` and `st.begun` (all item keys) are NOT on it. At drain start the keep list is empty. So an interrupted source `item.job` that a retry has re-read is swept on purpose when it differs from `read.job`: its old `target/` is dead weight, the retry starts from the base or from commits, never from that directory. When `item.job == read.job` (a queued item run as it stands) it is on the list through `read.job`. A job this drain held (a pre-producer hold) is skipped until the next drain start, which sweeps it.
decisions.reason: Read drain.rs:1222-1262 and :1325: `steps.run(&job)` gets `read.job`; `tried`/`begun` hold item keys. Other workers' in-flight jobs need no list entry: `go_job` holds their lock from before the Dispatched commit, so `try_lock_job` fails and they are skipped; the list only protects the drain's own just-finished or held jobs and the job about to run, as the brief says ('the drain's own jobs are skipped'). The Stub test asserts this choice (retry of 'x' gives `read.job` 'x-retry': own contains 'x-retry', not 'x').

risks.risk: The sweep removes a live job's build directory, or holds a lock a starting job needs.
risks.mitigation: Requires Dispatched in Records, no registry entry after `reap()`, a lock `try_lock_job` can take, and a job outside the keep list. `go_job` holds the lock before the Dispatched commit, so in-flight jobs are skipped by the lock. The guard test covers lock, registry, closed and keep cases.

risks.risk: An outside `athena retry X` or `athena go X` on an interrupted X while the sweep holds X's lock fails with 'already running in another athena process'.
risks.mitigation: The lock is held only while one `target/` is removed; a rerun succeeds. The drain's own just-run jobs are never locked by the sweep. Named in the CHANGELOG and docs.

risks.risk: The new pre-producer gate holds a job that previously ran, when free space is between the old checks' thresholds.
risks.mitigation: It uses the same `min_free_gb` and sweeps idle targets first, as the dispatch and check gates do; the default is unchanged. The hold is an environment stop with no attempt used, and a later drain retries the job.

risks.risk: `release_superseded_hold` clears the wrong job's marker, or hides a hold that still applies.
risks.mitigation: It clears only the source of a 'try again on X' request, only when X is Dispatched, not running, and has no resume mark; the late-hold path with a resume mark is untouched. It runs after the retry's prediction commit. The criterion 3 lifecycle assert covers the case.

risks.risk: A job held before the producer is Dispatched with no resume mark; the drain retries it as a new job from the base.
risks.mitigation: That is how any interrupted job without a candidate resumes. No candidate exists, so nothing is lost; the marker is cleared when the retry dispatches. The `go` message now says so.

risks.risk: A resumed interrupted job loses a build cache it could reuse.
risks.mitigation: Only `target/` is removed; the criterion 1 test asserts the work tree and kept work remain.

risks.risk: A Records read at drain start and before each run stalls or aborts the drain.
risks.mitigation: One load per sweep; an unreadable head or records prints a `warning:` line and returns 0 bytes. It never fails the drain.

risks.risk: The new trait method breaks existing `Steps` implementors; the Stub's new field breaks exact-log assertions.
risks.mitigation: A default no-op body keeps implementors compiling (tests/drain.rs has several); the Stub records calls in a separate field, not in `log`. Step 14 runs the whole workspace checks.

risks.risk: Existing run tests that count free-space reads or hold at the check gate change behavior with the new gate.
risks.mitigation: `built_then_low_disk` sets low space in the producer's script, after the new gate, so it still holds at the check gate. Step 14 runs all of them; the producer adjusts any assertion that relied on a read count.

demonstrations.method: Integration test through `drain::drain` with `RealSteps` and the production dispatch, producer and retry path. Space is low only after dispatch; a second drain with space free checks the hold's lifecycle.
demonstrations.observes: Setup: `disk_fixture()` (10 GB required), a Script counting `Role::Producer` calls in an `Arc<AtomicUsize>`, `athena.state.with_free_space(simulated_free)` with no `simulated_free` file (plenty), `queue_steward_request`, and a `Ui` wrapper over `Lines` that writes 3_000_000_000 into `<state>/simulated_free` on the first line starting `baseline`. First drain: `drain(&RealSteps{ui: &wrapper, ..}, work_everything(), &Quiet)`. Asserts: the item's outcome is `environment: low disk`, display text has `3.0 GB` and `10.0 GB`, `failed_item` is None, nothing landed; producer counter is 0; Records show the job H Dispatched with a job record, no outcome, no score (so it passed the dispatch gate); ui lines ordered `dispatched`, `baseline`, then `held       environment: low disk`; `disk::read_hold(H)` gives 3 GB / 10 GB; `display::status(&athena.status().unwrap())` shows `environment: low disk: 3.0 GB free, 10.0 GB required` on H; `athena.go(H)` errors with text that says it is read again and not 'resumes it from its kept candidate'; no line tells anyone to `athena retry`. Lifecycle (finding 1): delete `<state>/simulated_free` (plenty), run a second drain on the same Fixture: it retries H as a new job H2 and runs the producer (counter 1); then `disk::read_hold(H)` is None and the status text no longer shows H as held.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `producer_disk_gate` the producer runs (counter is 1) and the job is held only later by the check gate, so the first counter assert fails. If the hold were counted as a failure or committed an outcome, the outcome and Records asserts fail. Without `release_superseded_hold` the second-drain `read_hold(H)` is still Some and the lifecycle assert fails; without the `go` message change the message assert fails.

Every existing `Steps` implementor compiles against the defaulted `reclaim_interrupted`; the existing hold tests (`low_disk_*`, `the_real_steps_hold_a_job_on_low_disk_*`, `low_disk_after_the_build_holds_*`) and run/tests.rs disk tests (including the ones at tests.rs:1675, :1794, :1825 that read the hold marker) still pass with the new gate; no unused-import or dead-code warning.
demonstrations.fails_without: A missed fmt fails the first command; a badly shaped helper fails clippy; a `Steps` method without a default fails compilation; removing the reclaim calls or the gate turns the criterion 1, 2 and 3 tests red.
demonstrations.seam: The three cargo commands on the real workspace. No fake. Step 14 runs them.

demonstrations.observes: The diff adds `producer_disk_gate` in run/producer.rs and, in `produce_and_verify`, a call after `baseline_stage` and before `producer_snapshot` that returns `Err(self.hold_for_disk(ctx, closing, low))`. A search of the diff output for `#[path` and `tests/common` finds no added line in any src file.

demonstrations.method: Read the CHANGELOG and module-doc diffs.
demonstrations.command: git diff -- CHANGELOG.md crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs crates/athena-core/src/run/close.rs
demonstrations.observes: CHANGELOG.md gains an Unreleased bullet (Fixed group if present): root cause (an interrupted job's build directory was reclaimed only at dispatch or under low disk, so after a container restart it stayed until the disk filled and the next job failed), the fix (reclaim at drain start and before each run, work tree and candidate kept, the drain's own jobs skipped), the new disk check just before the producer that holds the job as an environment stop (not a failure, no attempt used), and that the retry spends the hold. No email or host name. drain.rs `//!` (interrupted-job bullet and 'Low disk holds a job' bullet), disk.rs `//!` (place list, 'Freeing and resuming') and the `hold_for_disk` doc describe the reclaim, its guards (Dispatched, no registry entry, lock free, own jobs kept, only `target/`) and the pre-producer check as a fourth place.

demonstrations.method: List changed paths and search the diff.
demonstrations.observes: Only crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs, crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs, crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs, crates/athena-core/src/run/close.rs (doc only) and CHANGELOG.md appear. No athena.toml or defaults.toml, no `min_free_gb` default line changed, and no removal of `work` or candidate paths (the only deletion calls added are `remove_target` and `clear_hold`).

open_questions: Send-back reruns of the producer are not gated (the gate runs once, before the first invocation); the gate before the checks still covers the built candidate. A gate on each rerun needs `producer_loop` to return the hold to a caller that owns `closing`; say so if wanted.

The test trigger relies on `baseline_stage` printing a line that starts `baseline` (read in producer.rs:59-71, `baseline   ...`) just before the new gate; if that changes, the test fails loudly (the producer would not be held).

Whether the second drain in the criterion 3 test retries H as a new job on the steward channel: drain.rs:59 says an interrupted job on a worked channel is retried, and `queue_steward_request` uses such a channel, but the second drain was not run; if the retry does not happen the producer adds a direct `athena.retry`-style request and runs `go` on it to reach the same dispatch.
